summary: The document describes a continuous-flow photoredox strategy for the decarboxylative monofluoroalkylation of Giese acceptors using 4CzIPN as a photocatalyst. The study includes optimization tables, scope schemes for various substrates and late-stage functionalization, and a multicomponent radical-polar crossover application.

items.heading: Scheme 1. (A) Examples of APIs Containing Monofluoroalkyl Groups. (B) Selected Strategies for the Generation of Monofluoroalkyl Radicals. (C) This Work Presents a Straightforward Methodology for the Streamlined Generation of Monofluoroalkyl Radicals from Readily Available α -Monofluorocarboxylic Acids
items.description: This scheme provides context on fluorinated drugs and compares the current decarboxylative approach with existing radical generation methods.

items.heading: Scheme 2. Development of a Direct Decarboxylative Monofluoroalkylation Strategy. (A) Design Plan of the Methodology. (B) Computational Studies on the Addition of 2a to Unsaturated Acceptors. (C) Calculated Global Electrophilicity Indices ( ω )
items.description: This scheme outlines the proposed catalytic cycle, computational energy barriers for radical addition, and electrophilicity indices of various radicals.

items.heading: Table 1. Optimization of Reaction Conditions in Batch
items.description: This table details the screening of photocatalysts, bases, solvents, light power, and reaction times to optimize the coupling of 2-fluoro-3-phenylpropanoic acid with benzyl methacrylate.

items.heading: Scheme 3. Photoredox Decarboxylative Monofluoroalkylation Strategy: α -Monofluorocarboxylic Acid and Giese Acceptor Scope
items.description: This scheme illustrates the substrate scope for various monofluorocarboxylic acids and Giese acceptors, including late-stage functionalization of complex molecules.

items.heading: Scheme 4. Mechanistic Investigations. (a) Radical Trapping Experiment. (b) Light On -Off Experiment
items.description: This scheme shows the results of TEMPO trapping and light-dark cycle experiments to support the radical nature of the mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 5. Photoredox-Catalyzed Three-Component Synthesis of Complex Fluorinated Structures via Multicomponent Radical-Polar Crossover in Continuous Flow
items.description: This scheme demonstrates the extension of the methodology to a three-component reaction involving an aldehyde to form highly functionalized fluorinated products.
